title: Other old-time drummers and his favorite
summary: Matthews brothers, Red Happy and Black Benny, and others; his favorite was Cottrell, who read the Red Book.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Were there any other drummers that were outstanding that you can remember when you were a boy that you liked especially?
Well, I liked it. Bebe. Matthews. Yeah, he was a drummer too. I liked it him. And Bill, he was pretty good too. Bill Matthews.
Bebe, best mostly in the dance band or on the street? What was he famous for?

The boys he played in the dance band. Dance band. I never remember him playing. But his brother Ramos, that's all he'd play. He never played in the dance band. Ramos. Ramos played in the street. Played in the street all the time. That's all he had. A snare, you know. I never remember. There ain't no one could play. You know, drop drums.
You ever hear of John McMurray or Diddy Chandler.
Oh, Diddy? Played trumpet? No. No. Another old time drummer. I think he played at Robichard. Chandler.
I know one fellow who used to call Ray, he down in Chicago.

Yeah, Red Hap. I never knew him. I've heard people know him. And another one used to play with him. He got killed. The woman killed him. Oh, Black Benny. Benny. Black Benny. I knew him. I knew them. He got killed.

Walter Brundy. Do you remember him? He was an old timer left here a long time ago. Who that? Walter Brundy. Probably before your time. No, I didn't know him. You see, there's John Veen. Did you know him? I didn't know him. John Veen. Mr. Henry Zeno. Is that another old guy? I know I know the past.
I know him. Who would be your favorite? Yeah, him. I know the past.

Yeah, I know the past days. Yeah, I know him. I know them good. Who would be your favorite drummers? Are your favorite drummer if you had to make a choice of one or two in the old days? Well, if I'd make a choice, a contral, only a contral was my favorite drum. From a kid coming up, oh, I didn't mind his drum. Yeah, he really knew what he was doing. Well, it's like I said, during that time, everybody had to know them tots, you know. Yeah, they had to know the music. Yeah, they had to know the music. Yeah. Because that's all they played, strictly music.
And they called that the Red Book, and that was hard, too. Because I know I played with them. I tried it, and I couldn't make it through that time. I was young, you know.
But it was hard. I know.
